title: Local scalar perfect models for dualizable condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$, and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_X[0]$. Dualizable means admitting a dual with evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities. The full subcategory of dualizable objects is stable: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts and distinguished cones.

Assume now that $X$ has Zariski locally finitely many irreducible components. An object $K$ of this derived category is dualizable if and only if there is a pro-etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ and, for each $i$, a perfect scalar complex $P_i\in D(R)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] such that
$$K|_{U_i}\simeq\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline{P_i}.$$
Here a perfect scalar complex is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules, underlines denote constant sheaves with discrete coefficients, and scalar extension uses the constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_{U_i}$. The complexes $P_i$ may vary with $i$. No regularity or flatness assumption on $\Lambda$ is imposed.

source.place: Definition 3.3(1) and the stable-subcategory observation immediately following it; Definition 3.5 and Theorem 4.13 (both directions).

proof.text: First establish stability, without any restriction on irreducible components. By [sk-thm-pe-weakly-contractible-basis] and [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality], it suffices to check a distinguished triangle on a w-contractible affine $U$. Write $A=\Gamma(U,\Lambda_U)$. The equivalence [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] writes any dualizable first and second terms as $F_U(P)$ and $F_U(Q)$ for perfect $A$-complexes, and represents the arrow by an arrow $P\to Q$ in $D(A)$. Choose bounded finite-projective representatives using [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] that arrow is represented by a chain map $p^\bullet\to q^\bullet$. Its cone has terms $q^n\oplus p^{n+1}$, again bounded and finite projective. Exactness of $F_U$ identifies its image with the third term of the triangle, which is therefore dualizable. The zero complex and integer shifts are likewise bounded finite-projective, and the equivalence preserves isomorphisms. Locality descends all these assertions to $X$.

source.place: Observation after Definition 3.3; Lemma 4.1(2); bounded-projective cone argument expanded

proof.text: We prove the implication from local scalar models to dualizability for every scheme, including cover objects with infinitely many irreducible components. For a perfect $P\in D(R)$ and any scheme $T$, cover $T$ by w-contractible affines $V$ using [sk-thm-pe-weakly-contractible-basis]. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\Lambda_V)$. By [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation], the restriction of $\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$ is $F_V(A\otimes_R^L P)$. A bounded finite-projective representative of $P$ computes this derived base change: each projective summand of $R^n$ becomes the corresponding summand of $A^n$. Thus $A\otimes_R^L P$ is perfect, even if $A$ is not flat over $R$, and its image under $F_V$ is dualizable. Apply [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality] first to this cover of $T$, and then to the given covering family of $X$. This proves the reverse implication with varying $P_i$.

source.place: Definition 3.5 and reverse implication of Theorem 4.13

proof.text: For the forward implication first suppose that $X$ is nonempty irreducible affine. Fix a geometric generic point $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$. Pullback preserves dualizability by [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality]. The affine geometric point is w-contractible (one strictly henselian local ring and one component), so [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] supplies $P\in\operatorname{Perf}(R)$ and $K|_\eta\simeq\Lambda_\eta\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$, since $\Gamma(\eta,\Lambda_\eta)=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)=R$. Choose an affine faithfully flat ind-etale w-contractible cover $U\to X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-source-wcontractible-extension]. For $S=\pi_0U$ the same evaluation lemma gives a dualizable $M\in D(S,\Lambda)$ with $\pi_U^*M\simeq K|_U$.

source.place: Theorem 4.13, first paragraph and irreducible case; geometric-point case of Lemma 4.1

proof.text:
Apply [lem-zl-generic-fiber-components-section] to $U\to X$ and $\eta$. With $S_\eta=\pi_0(U\times_X\eta)$ and $r:S_\eta\to S$, its commutative component square and the isomorphism at $\eta$ identify
$$r^*M\simeq\Lambda_{S_\eta}\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P.$$
Indeed their images under the coefficient-compatible equivalence $\pi_{U\times_X\eta}^*$ are respectively $K|_{U\times_X\eta}$ and the pullback of the scalar model at $\eta$; full faithfulness reflects the resulting isomorphism. Pull this isomorphism back along the continuous section $s:S\to S_\eta$. Inverse images on these profinite slice sites compose, $r\circ s=\mathrm{id}$, and the coefficient and constant-sheaf pullbacks are the specified ones. Thus $M\simeq\Lambda_S\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$. Applying $\pi_U^*$ and its scalar compatibility from [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] gives $K|_U\simeq\Lambda_U\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$. This proves the irreducible-affine case, with the very same $P$ on any such chosen cover.

source.place: Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the paragraph following it

proof.text: Now take an affine open $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ having finitely many irreducible components $X_a$. Give each component its reduced closed scheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], so $X_a=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_a)$ is irreducible affine. Their underlying sets cover $X$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. Pullback of $K$ to each $X_a$ is dualizable by [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality]. Choose an affine faithfully flat ind-etale w-contractible cover $W_a=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C_a\to X_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-source-wcontractible-extension]. Steps 3-4, applied over $X_a$ with this cover, give $K|_{W_a}\simeq\Lambda_{W_a}\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline{P_a}$ for a perfect $R$-complex $P_a$. Different components may give different $P_a$. We have made no claim that a closed subscheme of a w-contractible affine is w-contractible.

source.place: Theorem 4.13, finite-component paragraph, refined by w-contractible covers of the components

proof.text: Set $C_a=H_A(\overline C_a)$, using [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. Its diagram is filtered by [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered], so its defining colimit of etale $A$-algebras makes $C_a$ ind-etale over $A$. By [lem-exc-closed-lift-reduction] the specified map identifies $C_a/I_aC_a$ with $\overline C_a$. By [lem-zl-henselian-indetale-closed-lift] the pair $(C_a,I_aC_a)$ is henselian. Put $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$, with closed fiber $W_a$. Since $W_a$ is w-contractible, [lem-zl-condensed-henselian-lisse-rigidity] makes $V_a$ w-contractible and makes restriction $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(V_a,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{lis}}(W_a,\Lambda)$ fully faithful. Both $K|_{V_a}$ and its scalar model are dualizable: use [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality] for the former, and Step 2 for the latter. Full faithfulness lifts the isomorphism of Step 5 and its inverse; faithfulness makes their composites identities. We obtain $K|_{V_a}\simeq\Lambda_{V_a}\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline{P_a}$.

source.place: Theorem 4.13, finite-component paragraph; Bhatt--Scholze Definition 2.2.10, Lemma 2.2.12 and Lemma 6.1.1

proof.text: There are finitely many $a$. Each $V_a\to X$ is affine ind-etale, hence weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], so flat and a pro-etale site object. Its image contains all of $X_a$, since its closed fiber $W_a\to X_a$ is surjective. As the $X_a$ cover $X$, the finite affine disjoint union $\coprod_a V_a\to X$ is surjective, flat and quasi-compact, hence is a covering in the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The models of Step 6 therefore give the required covering. For a general $X$ with Zariski locally finitely many irreducible components, take affine open neighborhoods inside the open neighborhoods from that hypothesis. An open subset of a finite union of irreducible closed subsets has at most that finite number of irreducible components: intersect those subsets with the open and discard the empty ones. Apply the affine construction and compose the resulting covers with the Zariski open cover. The empty scheme uses the empty covering. No uniform amplitude, rank, or scalar model across cover members is required.

source.place: Theorem 4.13, Zariski localization and final covering argument
